titel: Cut A Worm In Half? Not Two Worms

beats.say: Cutting a worm in half... does *not* make two worms.
Maybe you *tried* it as a kid. Or your spade did it *for* you.
And you thought: no problem. Now there are *two.*
But a worm has a *front*, and a *back.*
That thick band, the *saddle*, sits close to the head.
Up front are its mouth, its tiny brain... and its *five hearts.*
Cut it in half, and the tail end can't grow a new *head.*
It wriggles for a while... and then it *dies.*
The head end *might* survive, if the cut is behind the saddle.
And often, it only grows back a *short*, stunted tail.
Live Science puts it simply: it will *not* become two new worms.
And worms are *gold* for your garden. They dig, mix and feed the soil.
Dig with a *fork*, not a spade, and go slowly.
Found a worm on top? Put it back on *damp soil*, out of the sun.
So next time your spade hits a worm... remember:
